title: Kingdom of the Gepids
capsule: The Gepids were an East Germanic people who participated in the Hunnic confederacy and gained their independence after defeating Attila's sons at the Battle of Nedao in 454, thereafter controlling Dacia (modern Transylvania and the Pannonian plain east of the Tisza). Their kingdom reached its height under King Cunimund in the mid-6th century, when Gepid Sirmium served as a prize contested with the Lombards and the Eastern Roman Empire. The Lombard king Alboin allied with the Avars and crushed the Gepids at the Battle of the Asfeld in 567, killing Cunimund; the Avars absorbed the Gepid population and territory, ending the kingdom.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Late antique written sources (Jordanes, Procopius) provide a reasonable political outline; Gepid territorial extent is reconstructed from archaeology and is approximate.
